perspective:
From Ethan’s perspective, he has access to:

- He is Ethan Mohamud, a plumber. Gary Guo is his long-time friend from middle school, now a doctor.
- He noticed Gary working excessively long hospital hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. This concerned him.
- He invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation. He heard Gary initially decline, saying he appreciated the concern but had too much to do at the hospital.
- During the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding talk about work. Ethan suspected there was more to Gary’s overworking than professional obligations.
- He confronted Gary as a middle-school friend, saying Gary could tell him anything. He heard Gary say it was complicated and that he didn’t want to burden Ethan.
- Gary then told Ethan about pressures managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan felt relief and empathy, and offered to help prioritize tasks and delegate responsibilities.
- Ethan heard Gary agree and say he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in, discussed Gary’s progress and challenges, saw Gary making efforts to change, felt hopeful and proud, and encouraged him. Gary told him things were better, he was less overwhelmed, and he had time for a movie.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary managing on his own and felt satisfied and happy. He told Gary he was always a call away but knew Gary had it. Gary thanked him, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and felt more in control.
